description:
You are a plant pathologist at an agricultural extension laboratory. A wheat farmer has submitted diseased crop samples, and your lab has sequenced the ITS (Internal Transcribed Spacer) region of the fungal pathogen isolated from the infected tissue. You must classify this unknown pathogen by comparing its ITS sequence against reference sequences from known wheat pathogens.

The data files are located at ~/UGENE_Data/agriculture/:
- unknown_pathogen_ITS.fasta: The ITS sequence from the farmer's diseased wheat sample
- reference_wheat_pathogens_ITS.fasta: ITS sequences from 10 known wheat fungal pathogens including Fusarium graminearum, Puccinia triticina, Blumeria graminis, Zymoseptoria tritici, Pyrenophora tritici-repentis, Tilletia caries, Ustilago tritici, Rhizoctonia cerealis, Gaeumannomyces tritici, and Bipolaris sorokiniana

Perform the following analysis in UGENE:

1. Open both FASTA files and combine all sequences (unknown + 10 references) into a single alignment view.

2. Perform a multiple sequence alignment using the ClustalW algorithm (not MUSCLE — ClustalW is standard for ITS-based fungal taxonomy). Use gap open penalty of 10 and gap extension penalty of 0.2.

3. Build a phylogenetic tree from the alignment using UGENE's phylogenetic tree builder. Select the Maximum Likelihood method (PhyML) with the HKY85 substitution model and 100 bootstrap replicates.

4. Save the alignment in PHYLIP format as ~/UGENE_Data/agriculture/results/pathogen_alignment.phy

5. Save the phylogenetic tree in Newick format as ~/UGENE_Data/agriculture/results/pathogen_tree.nwk

6. Save the alignment also in ClustalW format as ~/UGENE_Data/agriculture/results/pathogen_alignment.aln

7. Create a diagnostic report at ~/UGENE_Data/agriculture/results/pathogen_diagnosis.txt identifying which known pathogen the unknown sample clusters with based on the phylogenetic tree topology, the bootstrap support for that clade, and recommended management strategies for the identified pathogen.

metadata.data_source: Real ITS sequences from NCBI GenBank: PZ014411.1 (F. graminearum), PV098983.1 (P. triticina), PV416552.1 (B. graminis), MH862992.1 (Z. tritici), OQ257148.1 (P. tritici-repentis), MH855829.1 (T. caries), PV827756.1 (U. tritici), PV849335.1 (R. cerealis), MH855056.1 (G. tritici), PZ027992.1 (B. sorokiniana). Unknown sample is a modified F. graminearum ITS with 3 SNPs.
